steps.title: Draw one circle
steps.instruction: Type this short program and run it.
steps.explain: circle(78) draws a circle with a radius of 78. The turtle returns to its starting position and direction.
steps.expected: One pink circle on a dark background.
steps.question: Is 78 the full width?
steps.answer: No. It is the radius. The width is 156 units.
steps.help: Compare the changed lines with your editor. Check parentheses, commas, and quotation marks. Indent a loop or function body four spaces.

steps.title: Turn and draw another
steps.instruction: Turn the turtle, then repeat the circle.
steps.explain: The turtle starts at the same point, facing a new direction. That changes where the center of the next circle lies.
steps.question: Which command made the second circle land somewhere different?
steps.answer: left(20) changed the direction before drawing it.
steps.help: Compare the changed lines with your editor. Check parentheses, commas, and quotation marks. Indent a loop or function body four spaces.

steps.title: Repeat with a loop
steps.instruction: Replace the separate circles with a two-repeat loop.
steps.explain: Both circle() and left() are inside the loop. The turtle draws, turns, then does the same work again.
steps.expected: The same two circles. The last turn moves the pen direction without drawing.
steps.question: What if only circle(78) were indented?
steps.answer: Both circles would draw on top of each other, then the turtle would turn once.
steps.help: Compare the changed lines with your editor. Check parentheses, commas, and quotation marks. Indent a loop or function body four spaces.

steps.title: Complete a full turn
steps.explain: 18 × 20° = 360°. The circle positions spread all the way around the starting point.
steps.expected: A complete ring of overlapping pink circles.
steps.question: Why use 18 repeats with a 20-degree turn?
steps.answer: Eighteen 20-degree turns add up to one full turn.
steps.help: Compare the changed lines with your editor. Check parentheses, commas, and quotation marks. Indent a loop or function body four spaces.

steps.title: Make the pattern denser
steps.instruction: Use a smaller turn and enough repeats to total 360 degrees.
steps.explain: 90 × 4° = 360°. More circles fit into the same full rotation.
steps.expected: A denser pattern in the same overall area.
steps.question: Would 90 repeats with 20-degree turns give 90 different positions?
steps.answer: The direction repeats after every 18 turns, so many circles would overlap existing circles.
steps.help: Compare the changed lines with your editor. Check parentheses, commas, and quotation marks. Indent a loop or function body four spaces.

steps.title: Cycle through five colors
steps.instruction: Add the color list and select a color inside the loop.
steps.explain: i counts from 0. i % 5 gives the remainder after dividing by 5, so it cycles through 0, 1, 2, 3, 4. Those positions select the five colors. speed(0) draws this longer program instantly.
steps.question: Which list position is used when i is 7?
steps.answer: 7 % 5 is 2, so it uses the third color. List positions start at 0.
steps.help: Compare the changed lines with your editor. Check parentheses, commas, and quotation marks. Indent a loop or function body four spaces.

steps.nav: Let the list set the cycle
steps.title: Let the list set the cycle
steps.explain: len(colors) counts the list’s items. The cycle will still work if you later add or remove a color.
steps.expected: The same picture. This rewrite makes the color list easier to change.
steps.question: Why would leaving % 5 be a problem after shortening the list?
steps.answer: The loop could ask for a position that no longer exists.
steps.help: Compare the changed lines with your editor. Check parentheses, commas, and quotation marks. Indent a loop or function body four spaces.

steps.title: Finish with a center dot
steps.instruction: Lift the pen and add the small center detail.
steps.explain: penup() prevents a connecting line. dot(19) uses a diameter, so this dot is 19 units wide.
steps.expected: The finished multicolored pattern with a pale center dot.
steps.question: How is the input to dot() different from circle()?
steps.answer: dot() takes a diameter. circle() takes a radius.

steps.title: Make it yours
steps.instruction: Change one size, position, or color. Predict the result, then run. Try a second change after checking the first.
steps.explain: Keep your working program while you experiment. If an edit has an unexpected effect, undo that one edit and run again.
steps.question: Show a partner one edit. Why did that line change the picture?
steps.answer: Name the command, explain what its input controls, and point to the result.
